gaps.concept: ACTH-secreting pituitary adenoma causes Cushing disease: elevated ACTH and cortisol with central weight gain, proximal weakness, easy bruising, and purple striae.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with Cushing features and a pituitary lesion requires identifying the hormone-producing tumor.

gaps.concept: Pituitary ACTH secretion is usually suppressed by high-dose dexamethasone and stimulated by CRH; ectopic ACTH usually shows neither response.
gaps.why_tested: Dynamic endocrine tests distinguish Cushing disease from an ectopic ACTH source.

gaps.concept: Excess prolactin suppresses hypothalamic GnRH, lowering LH, FSH, and sex steroids.
gaps.why_tested: A prolactinoma stem asks why amenorrhea, infertility, sexual dysfunction, or bone loss occurs.

gaps.concept: Marked prolactin elevation favors prolactinoma; stalk compression usually causes a more modest elevation.
gaps.why_tested: Prolactin level helps distinguish a secreting adenoma from a nonfunctioning sellar mass.

gaps.concept: GH drives hepatic IGF-1 production; excess GH also causes insulin resistance.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which mediator produces tissue growth or why acromegaly causes hyperglycemia.

gaps.concept: Acromegaly can cause prognathism, frontal bossing, carpal tunnel syndrome, and obstructive sleep apnea.
gaps.why_tested: These clues identify GH excess when hand enlargement or the pituitary mass is unstated.

gaps.concept: Acromegaly is associated with colonic polyps.
gaps.why_tested: A vignette links a GH-secreting pituitary adenoma with an increased polyp burden.

gaps.concept: Octreotide is a somatostatin analog that suppresses GH secretion; gallstones are a characteristic adverse effect.
gaps.why_tested: A treatment vignette asks for the drug mechanism or adverse effect.

gaps.concept: Central adrenal insufficiency causes low ACTH and cortisol, often with hyponatremia; aldosterone and potassium are usually preserved, without hyperpigmentation.
gaps.why_tested: Hormone and electrolyte patterns distinguish pituitary ACTH loss from primary adrenal failure.

gaps.concept: Central hypothyroidism produces low free T4 with low or inappropriately normal TSH.
gaps.why_tested: A normal-range TSH can conceal pituitary hormone deficiency in a patient with a sellar lesion.

gaps.concept: Pituitary gonadotropin deficiency produces low LH/FSH and low sex steroids, causing amenorrhea or reduced libido.
gaps.why_tested: Paired gonadotropin and sex-steroid results distinguish central from primary gonadal failure.

gaps.concept: Central diabetes insipidus results from deficient posterior-pituitary ADH: polyuria, dilute urine, and possible hypernatremia.
gaps.why_tested: A sellar lesion with intense thirst and hypotonic polyuria points to posterior-pituitary dysfunction.

gaps.concept: In central diabetes insipidus, urine stays dilute during water deprivation but concentrates after desmopressin.
gaps.why_tested: A water-deprivation vignette distinguishes central diabetes insipidus from nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and primary polydipsia.

gaps.concept: Diabetes insipidus is unusual with a pituitary adenoma and favors a stalk or posterior-pituitary lesion such as craniopharyngioma.
gaps.why_tested: Polyuria helps discriminate among otherwise similar sellar masses.

gaps.concept: MEN1 is an autosomal dominant menin tumor-suppressor defect associated with pituitary adenomas, parathyroid tumors, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with a pituitary adenoma and other endocrine tumors prompts identification of the inherited syndrome.

gaps.concept: Adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma shows stratified squamous epithelium, peripheral palisading, and wet keratin.
gaps.why_tested: Histology of a calcified suprasellar mass identifies craniopharyngioma.

gaps.concept: The anterior pituitary arises from oral ectoderm via Rathke pouch; the posterior pituitary arises from neuroectoderm.
gaps.why_tested: An embryology question asks which tissue gives rise to a pituitary region or its tumor.

gaps.concept: Bitemporal hemianopia results from compression of crossing nasal retinal fibers in the optic chiasm.
gaps.why_tested: A visual-field diagram asks which fibers a suprasellar pituitary mass compresses.

gaps.concept: Lateral pituitary tumor extension into the cavernous sinus can cause ocular motor cranial nerve palsies.
gaps.why_tested: Diplopia or ptosis accompanying a sellar mass localizes extension beyond the sella.

gaps.concept: Empty sella occurs when CSF herniates through the diaphragma sellae and flattens the pituitary on imaging.
gaps.why_tested: An MRI showing a CSF-filled sella asks for the anatomic mechanism.

gaps.concept: Lymphocytic hypophysitis is autoimmune inflammation that can enlarge the pituitary or stalk and cause multiple pituitary hormone deficits.
gaps.why_tested: A peripartum patient with a sellar mass and new hypopituitarism may have inflammation rather than an adenoma.

gaps.concept: Prolonged exogenous glucocorticoid use suppresses CRH and ACTH; abrupt withdrawal can reveal secondary adrenal insufficiency.
gaps.why_tested: A patient becomes hypotensive after stopping steroids despite no primary adrenal disease.
